public_record: On 18 October 2023, at meeting S/PV.9442, the Security Council considered draft S/2023/773, submitted by Brazil, on the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question. It voted separately on two Russian amendments before voting on the draft. The draft received twelve votes in favour, one against and two abstentions. The United States voted against, and Russia and the United Kingdom abstained. The negative vote of a permanent member prevented adoption, so the draft created no new Council authority.
public_criteria: Identify the draft, Brazil as submitter and the agenda item.
Preserve the procedural sequence of two separate Russian amendments before the vote on the draft.
State the main tally and attribute the negative vote and both abstentions.
Distinguish the veto from passage and preserve the resulting limits of authority.

focuses.requester_card: Review S/2023/775. The chair counted six votes in favour, one against and eight abstentions. It fell short of the vote threshold. This was a separate amendment to the Brazilian draft.
focuses.backup: S/2023/775, proposed by Russia, would insert a paragraph after operative paragraph 2. It condemned indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian objects in Gaza, singled out the Al Ahli hospital strike, and condemned and rejected steps to impose a blockade depriving civilians of essentials.
focuses.requester_criterion: Report the 6–1–8 tally and failure to reach the required number of votes.
backup_criteria: Identify what document Russia proposed to amend and the insertion point after operative paragraph 2.
Preserve the proposed condemnation of indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian objects.
Attribute the particular reference to the Al Ahli hospital strike to the proposed text, with no inferred perpetrator.
Preserve the proposed condemnation of blockade steps that deprive the civilian population of essentials.

focuses.requester_card: Review S/2023/776. The chair counted seven votes in favour, one against and seven abstentions. It fell short of the vote threshold. This was a separate amendment to the Brazilian draft.
focuses.backup: Russia's S/2023/776 would insert an operative paragraph ahead of paragraph 1 of the Brazilian draft. It called for a humanitarian ceasefire that would begin immediately, endure and be fully observed.
focuses.requester_criterion: Report the 7–1–7 tally and failure to reach the required number of votes.
backup_criteria: Identify the Russian proposal and its insertion before operative paragraph 1.
Identify the proposed action as a humanitarian ceasefire.
Preserve both durability and full observance.

focuses.requester_card: Review the proposed aid provisions of Brazil's S/2023/773. The proposed provisions remained draft language because the Security Council vote did not adopt the instrument.
focuses.backup: Operative paragraph 7 of Brazil's S/2023/773 proposed humanitarian pauses for full, rapid, safe and unhindered access by United Nations humanitarian agencies and their implementing partners, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other impartial aid organizations. It also encouraged humanitarian corridors and other aid-delivery initiatives.
focuses.requester_criterion: Explicitly identify the aid proposals as part of the failed Brazilian draft.
backup_criteria: Identify operative paragraph 7 and distinguish the proposed pauses from the separate proposed ceasefire.
Preserve the full, rapid, safe and unhindered access qualifiers.
Preserve the coverage of UN agencies and implementing partners, the ICRC and other impartial humanitarian organizations.
Preserve the encouragement of corridors and other aid-delivery initiatives.

focuses.requester_card: Review the explanation of the United States' negative vote on the main draft. Any rationale in the supplement must be attributed to the U.S. representative, without inferring the reasons for either abstention.
focuses.backup: Speaking for the United States after the vote on S/2023/773, Linda Thomas-Greenfield objected that the draft omitted Israel's right of self-defence. She invoked Article 51 of the UN Charter and argued the Council should have reaffirmed that right in the text.
focuses.requester_criterion: Identify the statement as the U.S. explanation concerning its vote on the main, vetoed draft.
backup_criteria: Attribute the statement to Linda Thomas-Greenfield speaking for the United States.
State that she objected to the draft's omission of Israel's right of self-defence.
Identify Article 51 as the Charter provision she cited.
Record that she wanted the text to reaffirm that right, with the view remaining attributable to her.

guard: Fail for confusing amendment numbers, tally, insertion position or disposition; calling either sub-threshold amendment a veto; treating failed proposals as Council action; presenting a national assertion as a Council finding; or adding a historical claim beyond the delivered evidence.

simulation.question: Can you send the certified working file for this review?
simulation.scope: Retrospective two-desk simulation. The requester sees a single focal card and forwards it to the chair over a protected channel. The responder sees an unordered pair of substantive backups. The same generic certified-file request may be sent or withheld, and the requested file is unavailable in all worlds. What the desk lacks is simulated, not historical. The request can act as a learned signal. The chair always receives an identical common record.
